# L-lyxose finalization serialization successor v3

The exact v2 assembly was rejected by the native validator before any save.
Its 111 edge assessments reuse evidence-ID list objects in two places. PyYAML
`safe_dump` emitted 111 anchors and 111 aliases; the native loader deliberately
rejects both. This is a serialization defect, not a scientific payload defect.

`assemble_review.py` now calls the unchanged native `record_review.py`
`_dump_document` function through a small `runpy` wrapper. That serializer already
suppresses aliases and is the one used by native save. The only operational code
delta is the import, wrapper, and replacement dump call in `exact-diff.patch`.
All other operational modules, guards, contracts, targets, and accepted bindings
are byte-identical to v2. Main-function AST equality is checked after normalizing
only that dump call. No schema, source identity, assessment, scientific statement,
review independence, issue disposition, review provenance, or receipt guard changes.

Seven serialization tests passed. They reproduce the actual 111 anchors/aliases,
prove full payload roundtrip equality and native validation, test shared nested
lists/maps, retain rejection of aliases/anchors/explicit tags, compare the complete
main-function AST and unchanged operational modules, and rehash all 173 protected
original files. All 47 inherited lineage/guard fixtures passed unchanged. The
actual native CLI `record_review.py validate serialization-preview.yaml` also
exited zero. Initial lint-only failures and their corrected rerun are retained.

`serialization-preview.yaml` is an exact semantic reserialization of the failed
payload for diagnosis and validation only. It is not a new inspector run or an
assembly receipt and must not be treated as a saved review. Root should rerun the
v3 assembler to obtain current inspection and fresh assembly receipts, then use
all remaining v3 entrypoints. Do not mix a v2 assembly with v3 lineage consumers:
the exact helper path in the actual inspector command is intentionally verified.

Root execution, after independent acceptance:

```sh
env PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 UV_NO_SYNC=1 /private/tmp/pathwaymech-next-195-20261011/.venv/bin/python -B /private/tmp/pathwaymech-next-227-finalization-v3-20261012/assemble_review.py --archive-receipt /private/tmp/pathwaymech-next-227-finalization-archive-applied-20261012.json --output /private/tmp/pathwaymech-next-227-native-review-assembly-v3-20261012
```

Use `run_native.py`, `archive_completion.py`, `bind_final_files.py`, and
`seal_completion.py` from this v3 directory, with fresh external output paths and
root's explicit `--apply` where required. The unchanged full receipt sequence is
in `predecessor-v2/README.md`. V3 preserves all five native receipt checks,
inspection/config/archive closure, input/current-file checks, complete archive
requirements, and the post-save inventory/preservation chain. The full predecessor
package and failed original assembly/run are retained in the sealed ancestry and
will be included by the unchanged completion archive implementation. Original
external directories remain byte-identical.

No maintained, Git, shared cache, or installation writes were performed. Native
save/history/commit/PR/merge/cleanup remain root-owned. This is the serialization
successor author's bounded verification, not independent approval of its own fix
or a new all-literature scientific review. Source exhaustion is false.
